all.explanation_html:
The rating is Elo, as in chess. A win raises it and a loss lowers it, and beating a higher-rated name moves it more. The exact rule follows.

Each person or group starts with a rating of 1500. Before a vote, let RA and RB be the two ratings. Elo's expected score for A is:

E_A = 1 / (1 + 10^((R_B − R_A) / 400))
E_B = 1 − E_A

A win gives S = 1, a loss S = 0, and a draw S = ½. The two sides' outcomes sum to one. With K = 32, both ratings are updated as follows:

R′_A = R_A + 32(S_A − E_A)
R′_B = R_B + 32(S_B − E_B)

Both expected scores and both updates use the ratings from before the vote. Updating A first does not change the values used for B. An unexpected win moves the ratings more than an expected win; a draw brings unequal ratings closer together. Daily 10 and Random votes both update these ratings. Skips do not count. The table orders everyone with at least one vote by their current rating.

all.explanation_html:
Foresight score: points for picks the crowd underrated when you made them, and later came around to. The exact rule follows.

All time counts every vote: Random votes and Daily 10 votes from every date, including unfinished and shared-seed sets. Someone who isn't signed in is listed under a generated name, and signing in moves the current tab's eligible votes to their account.

For each vote, p is the chance Elo gave your pick when you voted and q is the chance it gives now. Both leave out the push your own votes gave the two ratings, and both are held between 0.02 and 0.98. The vote earns, in bits:

b = log₂(q / p)

A pick at 20% that now stands at 80% earns 2 bits; a favorite that stays where it was earns 0; a pick the crowd moved away from loses bits. A draw counts as half a vote for each side. A vote counts once it is settled: both contenders have had 20 votes from other people since, or it is 3 days old. Your bits are averaged with a weight of 10 votes at 0, so a handful of votes counts for little, and the average b̄ is put on a scale from 0 to 100:

Foresight = 100 / (1 + 2^(−25 b̄))

50 means as good as the crowd; above 50, the crowd came round to your picks. Equal scores are ordered by more votes first, then name. A dash means no vote has settled yet. Votes are saved; the score is recalculated whenever it is shown and can change as other people vote.
